clue.text: Abandon TV and toy

parts.note: to jack in a job is to give it up, British slang for abandon
the box is a colloquial name for television

explanation.surface: Someone gives up watching television and turns to playthings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack in' is British slang for quit, and 'the box' is the television set.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a children's toy where a figure springs out of a lidded box.

clue.text: Dieter's OK source of minerals, eating small plant

indicators.note: the pair takes the small letter in between them

parts.note: Dieter is a German name, and ja is German for yes
minerals are dug from a mine

explanation.surface: A slimmer approves of a mineral-rich plant on their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dieter' looks like a slimmer, but it is a German man's name, so his OK is the German word for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasmine is a climbing shrub with fragrant white or yellow flowers.

clue.text: Snappy mongrel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: irritable, inclined to snap at people
second meaning: a ...-breed, a hybrid animal

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it pictures a bad-tempered dog, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means angry as an adjective and a hybrid of breeds as a noun.

clue.text: Episodes cut short when handling depression

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the depression in its hands, around it
the word for cut is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to incise is to cut into
a dent is a hollow, a depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Accounts of episodes curtailed when someone handles a low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood but is a dent in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidents are occurrences or events, as episodes are.

clue.text: Served up hot lush rhubarb

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are presented going upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker, a sot

explanation.surface: Someone served a hot drunkard a rhubarb pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' is the food in the picture but is used in its British sense of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is nonsense, and rhubarb is British slang for meaningless talk.

clue.text: Bearing object on uniform, item of jewellery

indicators.note: in a down clue the object sits on top of the letter for uniform

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A soldier wearing a badge on a uniform along with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Enduring means tolerating or putting up with something, as bearing it does.

clue.text: Wooden old rack being regularly used

indicators.note: only letters at regular intervals in these two words are used, every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are taken

explanation.surface: An old wooden rack still in regular use.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken means made of oak, a kind of timber.

clue.text: Less amenable ostrich, stern having wings totally clipped

indicators.note: both words lose their outer letters at each side, as a bird's two wings are cut off

parts.note: the word as written, trimmed at both ends
the word as written, trimmed at both ends

explanation.surface: A grumpy ostrich with a severe look and wings fully cut back is harder to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings are the outside letters: OSTRICH gives STRIC and STERN gives TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricter means more severe or rigid, so less easy-going and less willing to comply.

clue.text: Hunted and restrained, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: chaste means pure and restrained in behaviour

explanation.surface: An animal pursued and held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Chased means pursued, as prey is when hunted.

clue.text: Sold! Cashew nuts not left displayed

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged
not tells us to drop the letter for left from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written before the L is dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: An auctioneer's cry over a lot of cashews, with nothing left to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To showcase something is to exhibit it prominently, so showcased means put on display.

clue.text: Wiping up from sauce vessel

indicators.note: wiping something off removes it, so the word up is erased from the sauce

parts.note: ketchup is a tomato sauce
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mopping up a spill of sauce from a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiping up' reads as cleaning; it actually means the word UP is wiped out of the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat, a kind of seagoing craft.

clue.text: Some assassins identified using secret source

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: inside information comes from a confidential contact

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these two words are taken, the run spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some hired killers were tracked down thanks to an informant.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside describes knowledge or a job carried out with help from a confidential insider.

clue.text: Tradename is on outside of energy drinks

parts.note: a brand is a trade name

indicators.note: the word is wraps around the letter for energy, sitting on its outside

explanation.surface: A trade name printed around an energy drink's can.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandies are spirits distilled from wine, so they are alcoholic beverages.

clue.text: Give more detail of Times article on page occupying editor

indicators.note: these letters take up residence between the two letters of the editor abbreviation
in an across clue the article comes after the page, placed on it

parts.note: the times sign in arithmetic is X
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Times article is placed on a page while an editor asks for more detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper here but the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand on a point is to develop it further, adding more explanation.

clue.text: Soldier, man crossing a foreign land

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: the man lies across the A, with it sitting inside him

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A soldier and another man crossing into a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraguay is a landlocked country in South America.

clue.text: Excited with hosting international friend

indicators.note: the word for with plays host, holding the other letters inside it

parts.note: and means together with
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be welcoming an overseas friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means lively and full of spirit, as an excited person is.

clue.text: Factory operator's computer is crushed in tip

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

indicators.note: the word is is squeezed into the middle of the tip

parts.note: a hint is a tip

explanation.surface: A factory worker's computer has been smashed at the rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a rubbish dump (British sense), but is a helpful hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist operates machines, typically in a factory or workshop.

clue.text: Bleach expired unfortunately, tackling nothing

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take on, and so enclose, the zero
things going unluckily suggest a mix-up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bottle of bleach has gone past its date, so it is no use.
explanation.definitionFit: Peroxide is hydrogen peroxide, used as a hair bleach.

clue.text: Richest criminal adopts new name

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take on the extra letter, which joins at the end
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: The wealthiest crook takes on a fresh alias.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen is to give a name to, as at baptism or when naming a ship.

clue.text: Military unit firm and sharp to limit resistance

indicators.note: the word for sharp sets limits on both sides of the resistance letter

parts.note: hot food has a sharp, spicy taste

explanation.surface: A firm and keen unit keeping resistance under control.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was a division of a Roman legion, a body of troops.

clue.text: Insect starts to sting champion horse

indicators.note: the starting letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: the first letters of sting and champion
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A beetle starts to sting a prize-winning racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Request to enter wagers for goals in ball game

indicators.note: the request goes into the wagers

parts.note: bets are wagers
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone asks to place bets on the scoring in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: In basketball, points are scored by putting the ball through the hoops, also called baskets.

clue.text: Scholarly sign of incredulity?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: intellectual, of refined learning
second meaning, cryptic: a ... is an eyebrow raised in disbelief

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, playful reading: someone who doubts you raises their brow high.
explanation.definitionFit: Highbrow describes intellectual or cultured tastes, while a raised eyebrow shows disbelief.

clue.text: Dessert is lots of money, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: a bomb is British slang for a large sum, as in to cost a bomb

explanation.surface: A pudding that costs a fortune, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a frozen dessert of ice cream moulded into a dome.

clue.text: Tiny creatures team found in pastries

indicators.note: the team is discovered sitting inside the pastries

parts.note: pies are pastries
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Little creatures and a sports team discovered inside pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixies are small mischievous fairies of folklore.

clue.text: Picture that is covering publication

indicators.note: the two letters cover the publication on either side

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a mag is a magazine

explanation.surface: A photograph used on the cover of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or visual representation.

clue.text: Ancient structure of stone and woad uncovered

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for the stone, a British unit of weight

indicators.note: its covering letters at each end are stripped off

parts.note: loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: An old monument built of stone and painted blue with woad.
explanation.walkthrough: Woad is a blue dye the ancient Britons used.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade of ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Half of Spanish football team leaving field

indicators.note: only the first half of the club's name is kept, the rest left off

parts.note: Real Madrid is a famous Spanish football club

explanation.surface: Half of the Real Madrid side walks off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like the football pitch, but it is the definition, in the sense of a sphere of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or area of knowledge, as a field of study is.

clue.text: Rebuilt it, nice art complex

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the pieces together again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An arts complex has been rebuilt with attractive features.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means very detailed and complicated, as something complex is.

clue.text: Patron's complaint about new player

indicators.note: the complaint goes round the letter for new

parts.note: a beef is a grievance or complaint
an actress is a stage player

explanation.surface: A patron grumbles about a new performer in the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactress is a woman who gives money or support, a female patron.
